posts.title: [TEST] Why we think a rupee a day from many people can pay for the open source that India runs on
posts.excerpt: A long post with a long title and no lead image. It shows how a real article reads: sections, a list, a quote and links, but no images at all.

children.text: We started The Rupee Fund with one question: what would it take for people in India to back the open source projects they use every day? This post is a test, but it reads like a real post, so the page can show how a long article feels.

Most people who use open source never pay for it. That is not because they do not care. Paying is hard, the amounts feel too small to matter, and nobody asks. A fund that pools many small amounts changes each of those things.
A rupee a day is not much on its own. From ten thousand people, it pays a maintainer for a year. The
matters more than the size of each amount.
We look for projects that many people in India depend on, and that have few other ways to get money. We read the code, talk to the maintainers and ask the community. The
The project is open source, under a licence that the
People in India build it, or many people in India use it.
The money changes what the maintainers can do.
We are collecting a list of people who want to take part. We take no money yet. When we are ready, we will write to each person on the list with the details.
Open source is how India builds software. It is time we paid for it.
Thank you for reading this far. Send us your questions at

peoplePage.teamIntro: Meet the volunteers from the FOSS United community who run The Rupee Fund and maintain this website.
peoplePage.joinBody: Bring ideas, skills, and a little time to the community team, or introduce someone who will.

children.text: The FOSS United Foundation is the fiscal host of The Rupee Fund and supports the wider FOSS United community. Meet the

people.name: Shree Kumar
people.bio: Shree (Kumar) is an active volunteer at FOSS United and was formerly an elected member of its Governance Board. Shree helps run IndiaFOSS, arguably India's largest volunteer run conference dedicated to Free and Open Source Software, Hardware, and the wider digital commons.

people.name: Mrugesh Mohapatra
people.bio: Mrugesh is an active member of the FOSS United community and organises meetups for the Agentic AI Foundation’s Bengaluru Chapter.

people.name: Khitab
people.bio: Khitab is a FOSS United volunteer who builds and maintains The Rupee Fund’s website. He’s a data engineer drawn to how open source underpins India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and Digital Public Goods (DPG).
